profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting between an engineering manager and a developer experience lead at a mid-sized SaaS company that is preparing a six-week pilot to improve documentation practices across agile teams. The company recently circulated a systematic literature review on documentation in agile software development, and leadership wants a practical pilot focused on the checkout area before the next quarterly planning cycle. The agenda is to decide what the pilot includes, what artifacts need to be prepared, which tooling approach to use, who owns each workstream, and what counts as a successful pilot by the end of the quarter. The expected outcome is a shared implementation plan for the pilot, including scope, deliverables, ownership, and timeline.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.expertise: Team planning, cross-squad delivery, operational readiness, agile process adoption
members.background: Priya manages three backend squads that support cart, checkout, and payments services, and she is responsible for making sure internal process improvements do not disrupt the quarter's feature commitments.
members.private_state: Priya wants the pilot to look concrete and low-risk in time for quarterly reporting, avoid pulling too many engineers off roadmap work, and produce visible artifacts leadership can point to as progress.
hidden_assumptions: When people say a documentation 'baseline,' they mean a minimum required set of documents each service should have in place.
A pilot on the 'checkout flow' should stay within the squad boundary of the Checkout service so ownership remains clean.
If documentation pages exist, are linked from the README, and have been reviewed once by squad leads, that is enough to call the pilot done.
The 'existing templates' are the Confluence page templates already used for architecture notes and runbooks across platform teams.
Documentation improvements should fit around current sprint commitments rather than introducing automation work that creates new engineering tasks.

members.name: Lucas Chen
members.expertise: Developer tooling, docs-as-code workflows, engineering enablement, documentation systems
members.background: Lucas leads internal efforts to improve engineering effectiveness and has recently been advocating for documentation workflows that stay synchronized with code changes through templates and repository-based checks.
members.private_state: Lucas wants this pilot to validate a repeatable documentation system, prove that synchronization matters more than static pages, and create a model he can scale to other product areas afterward.
hidden_assumptions: When people say a documentation 'baseline,' they mean the current-state inventory and measurement snapshot used to compare pilot impact later.
The 'checkout flow' naturally means the end-to-end customer purchase path, including cart, pricing, checkout, and payments touchpoints.
A documentation pilot is only truly done if the docs are embedded in the engineering workflow and stay updated through at least one normal sprint change.
The 'existing templates' are the docs-as-code starter templates that Developer Experience quietly piloted in two repos last month.

Because leadership asked for documentation practices informed by the literature review, it is already accepted that the pilot should emphasize synchronization between tools and artifacts, not just document creation.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'set the baseline in the first week.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means defining and creating the minimum required documentation set for the pilot area: README links, a runbook, and an architecture note.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas means capturing the current documentation state and coverage metrics before any changes are made so they can measure improvement afterward.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both meanings sound reasonable in a planning meeting, and 'baseline' is a standard improvement-program term that rarely gets unpacked unless someone notices timeline inconsistencies.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the 'checkout flow' pilot
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the pilot will focus on 'the checkout flow.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya assumes the pilot covers the Checkout service team's own repositories and supporting docs, because that is the manageable unit for staffing and delivery.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas assumes the pilot covers the full user-facing checkout path across Cart, Pricing, Checkout, and Payments because documentation should follow the value stream users experience.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'checkout flow' is common in product and engineering conversations, and each person's interpretation feels like the obvious one from their role, so neither expects ambiguity.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as 'done' for the pilot
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree they want the pilot 'done by the end of the quarter.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means the target docs exist, are linked in the right places, and have enough review signoff that leadership can see the pilot completed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas means the docs are not only created but also wired into normal development so a code change during the pilot updates or validates documentation through the workflow.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both participants use the same completion language and both care about quality, but they silently apply different thresholds for what qualifies as a finished documentation improvement.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'existing templates' they plan to use
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'reuse the existing templates so we do not start from scratch.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya is referring to the established Confluence templates for architecture decisions, service overviews, and incident runbooks.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas is referring to the repository-based markdown templates and CI checks from the recent Developer Experience starter kit.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both template sets are genuinely existing within the organization, and because each person mainly interacts with one of them, the phrase sounds fully specific without actually identifying the same artifact.

turns.inner_thought: Leadership wants something they can point to in quarter-end reporting, and I need this to look real without derailing feature delivery. If we lock a tight scope, clear owners, and a simple timeline, I can keep the Checkout squad doing a small amount of documentation work around their existing sprint commitments and avoid creating a new engineering project.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. Leadership wants a six-week pilot coming out of the agile-documentation review, and I'd like us to leave today with scope, owners, and timing locked so the teams can start cleanly next week.

turns.inner_thought: Good, this is a chance to prove the pilot should be about documentation staying in sync with work, not just producing a handful of pages. If I can get even one area to show docs moving with normal development, that gives me a reusable model for the rest of engineering.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. I'd love to use the pilot to show that documentation can stay synchronized with day-to-day agile work instead of becoming another static artifact set people forget about.

turns.inner_thought: The safest choice is the Checkout service boundary. That's a squad I can actually ask to own this without dragging Cart and Payments into a cross-team exercise. And week one should be used to define and stand up the minimum required docs set so everyone knows what exists and what still needs filling in.
turns.utterance: Agreed. I think we should focus the pilot on the checkout flow and get the baseline in place during the first week so the squads have something concrete to work from.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect. I'll treat the checkout flow as the full purchase path and capture where docs stand today across the services involved. If I inventory current coverage and map it to the factors from the literature review, we'll have a solid baseline to compare against later.
turns.utterance: Yes, that works. I can inventory what exists today across the checkout flow and compare it against the factors from the review to establish that baseline quickly.

turns.inner_thought: I do not want net-new tooling work. We already have Confluence templates for architecture notes, service overviews, and runbooks; the squad leads know them, and using those keeps this lightweight. The easiest path is for each squad to fill in missing pages during the next sprint without changing how they build software.
turns.utterance: Good. To keep setup light, let's reuse the existing templates so we do not start from scratch, and then have each squad fill in the missing pieces during the next sprint.

turns.inner_thought: Great, she's open to the starter kit. I can put the repo-based templates and checks into the pilot repos up front so docs updates happen as part of normal code changes. That's exactly the kind of embedded workflow the review was pointing toward, and it will help us say the pilot is really done by the end of the quarter.
turns.utterance: Great, I can wire the existing templates into the pilot repos first so updates happen naturally as engineers touch checkout-related code.

turns.inner_thought: I need one clear owner, and that should be the Checkout squad lead. Cart and Payments can sanity-check anything that touches them, but I don't want this to become a multi-team program. Keeping it contained is the only way we can say it's done by the end of the quarter without hurting roadmap work.
turns.utterance: On ownership, I'd like the Checkout squad lead to be the primary owner, with Cart and Payments reviewing where needed. That keeps the pilot contained enough to be done by the end of the quarter.

turns.inner_thought: I can work with that as a practical entry point, but for the checkout flow to make sense I still need the service owners along the path involved enough to align the handoffs. Otherwise the end-to-end view will stay fragmented and we won't learn much that scales.
turns.utterance: Sounds good. I'll coordinate with the service owners along the flow so the handoffs and dependencies are documented consistently end to end.

turns.inner_thought: I should make the success criteria explicit so there isn't pressure to keep extending this. For quarter-end, I just need the pages created, linked from the service entry points, and reviewed once by the leads. That is tangible, low-risk, and easy to report upward as complete.
turns.utterance: For success at quarter-end, I want the docs in place, linked from the service entry points, and reviewed once so the pilot can be reported as complete.

turns.inner_thought: That's a good visible milestone, but I also need at least one ordinary sprint change to exercise the workflow. If a normal code update goes through and the documentation path works without extra heroics, then we can honestly say the pilot was done by the end of the quarter and that the system is sustainable.
turns.utterance: Agreed. And if one normal change goes through before quarter-end with the documentation path working smoothly, I think we'll have a strong pilot outcome.

turns.inner_thought: I'll have the Checkout lead start assembling the minimum doc set on Monday: README links, a runbook, and an architecture note. If we have that initial pack ready by the next sprint review, leadership will see momentum and the squad won't lose too much delivery time.
turns.utterance: Perfect. I'll ask the Checkout lead to start the baseline next Monday, and I want the initial documentation pack ready by the following sprint review.

turns.inner_thought: I'll prep the starter templates and collect the before-state snapshot this week so we can start measuring immediately. Once the pilot kicks off, I can help the repos adopt the workflow with minimal friction and have evidence of improvement by the end.
turns.utterance: Great. I'll prepare the template setup and baseline snapshot this week so the pilot can start on schedule.
